transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-02
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (AE), Samir Patel (SE), Lena Ortiz (CSM), Ravi Shah (SE), Maya Thompson (Procurement), Dr. Alan Reyes (CTO), Priya Nair (Legal), Carlos Mendez (Head of Data Security)

Summary (auto):
Quick procurement review focused on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, data residency and onboarding timeline. Customer wants private deployment options for PHI, clarifications on KMS/HSM and audit logs, and a pricing threshold for going to Dedicated. Agreed next steps to exchange redlines, schedule pilot benchmark, and finalize regions.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redlines and liability caps
- Data residency and private deployment (VPC/on-prem)
- SLAs: uptime, latency SLOs, incident response
- Security: SOC 2, encryption at rest/transit, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC
- Pricing and pilot scope for Dedicated vs Hosted
- Onboarding runbook and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intros — i'm Jamie from Redwood, AE on the account. we have Samir and Ravi from engineering and Lena on CSM.
[00:10] Maya Thompson: thanks, Jamie. Maya here from procurement. we wanted to go through the MSA/DPA redlines and make sure the SLA language matches what our security team needs.
[00:18] Dr. Alan Reyes: Alan, CTO. hi. main thing for us is PHI handling, data residency, and the ability to run private deployments.
[00:25] Samir Patel: great, thanks. i'll kick off with a quick technical overview of modes — hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (vpc / on-prem) — and then we can map that to the legal asks.
[00:36] Samir Patel: so hosted is our fastest path but data goes through redwood's control plane; dedicated is isolated GPU pools with stronger tenancy and egress controls; private gives you customer-managed network, bring-your-own-keys if you need HSM integration.
[00:48] Carlos Mendez: when you say bring-your-own-keys, do you mean full HSM integration with rotating keys and no key material leaving our environment?
[00:56] Ravi Shah: yes, for private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, and we can put in an agreement that key material never leaves the customer's control plane. open to working with your KMS vendor for a technical run.
[01:08] Priya Nair: on the DPA side we flagged the standard limitation of liability section and wanted more clarity on breach notification windows — specifically 48 vs 72 hours — and whether you provide forensic logs/audit trails for at least 12 months.
[01:22] Jamie Park: understood. we typically offer 72 hour notification in hosted SLAs but for enterprise private contracts we can negotiate 48 hours. audit logs — we retain platform-level audit logs by default 12 months for Dedicated/Private; can extend as an add-on.
[01:36] Maya Thompson: OK, procurement will want 48 hours and 12 months of logs as baseline. also need SOC 2 report and attestations.
[01:43] Samir Patel: we can produce SOC 2 and ISO attestations; we also provide architecture diagrams and pen-test summaries under NDA.
[01:52] Dr. Alan Reyes: latency SLOs — our product needs sub-200ms p50 for embeddings at low volumes, and we need throughput guarantees for batch scoring. how does Dedicated differ on that?
[02:04] Samir Patel: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and pinned capacity so you get consistent latency; we can publish per-model performance profiles and pin models/versions. for p50 <200ms on embeddings we'll need to benchmark your workload — sequence lengths, batch sizes, concurrency — during the pilot.
[02:19] Carlos Mendez: about data residency, we operate in US-only regions for PHI; can you guarantee all processing and logs remain in us-east-1 or our private VPC?
[02:28] Ravi Shah: yes, with Private deployment we can ensure processing happens only in your VPC; for Dedicated we can pin region and limit replication. we'll need to capture region list in the SOW.
[02:37] Priya Nair: liability cap — we have a preferred cap tied to one year of fees, not aggregate; typical redwood language is lower. procurement would like to see that changed.
[02:46] Jamie Park: understood; our standard is aggregate or per-event? we can take that as a negotiation item — i will send redline suggestions and legal can iterate.
[02:54] Maya Thompson: great. on pricing, we need a threshold that triggers moving from Hosted to Dedicated — like if monthly spend hits $X we want the option for reserved capacity pricing.
[03:05] Lena Ortiz: we can model that. Typically we show reserved capacity breaks at commit tiers; we can run a cost comparison for your projected monthly tokens/embedding calls and show when Dedicated is cheaper.
[03:16] Dr. Alan Reyes: one more security question — do you support SSO/SAML + SCIM for provisioning? we need central RBAC mapped to our LDAP/Okta.
[03:25] Samir Patel: yes, SSO/SAML + SCIM for user provisioning; role-based access controls are configurable and we hook into Okta groups. audit logging ties back to actions.
[03:34] Priya Nair: also need to confirm retention of transcripts and whether any customer content is used for model training by Redwood.
[03:40] Jamie Park: short answer: for enterprise/private deployments we offer a contract clause prohibiting use of customer content for model training. Hosted has an opt-out option; we'll add explicit terms in the DPA.
[03:50] Carlos Mendez: ok good. secondarily, can you provide an SLA for incident response times and a defined escalation path? procurement wants a 4-hour initial response for Sev1 and a dedicated Slack channel for on-call.
[04:01] Ravi Shah: we can commit to response SLA in enterprise packages; dedicated slack channel and a named escalation contact is standard for enterprise. we'll document the on-call rotation in the SOW.
[04:12] Maya Thompson: about the DPA — our legal flagged a clause around subcontractors and asked for a list of subprocessors and whether you allow subprocessing outside the US.
[04:22] Jamie Park: we'll provide the current list of subprocessors and limit to US regions for PHI; any changes to subprocessors are notified per agreement. for private deployments, we minimize subprocessors.
[04:33] Priya Nair: can you confirm data deletion timelines post-contract? we require 30 days complete purge and certificate of destruction.
[04:41] Samir Patel: we support data export and deletion; standard is 30 days for Hosted/Dedicated and immediate for Private since data sits in your VPC — we can provide a certificate of deletion for Hosted/Dedicated as a term.
[04:52] Dr. Alan Reyes: logistics for pilot — we want a 2-week benchmark with our sample load (embedding + rerank) and to validate p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k requests. what environment do you need from us?
[05:05] Ravi Shah: we'll need a sample dataset, expected concurrency, sequence sizes, and access to your VPC if private. Samir will draft the benchmark plan and cost estimate.
[05:15] Jamie Park: quick recap — we'll send redlined MSA/DPA, include 48 hour notification and 12 months audit logs as requested, provide SOC2/ISO docs under NDA, and Samir will send the benchmark plan. Lena will share onboarding runbook. any other items?
[05:28] Maya Thompson: procurement wants the redline by the 6th. we'll review and come back with consolidated comments.
[05:33] Priya Nair: legal will review the redline and revert by the 9th.
[05:36] Jamie Park: great. we can target pilot week of July 13th. we'll follow up on calendar invites and the SOW.
[05:41] Lena Ortiz: i'll prepare the onboarding checklist, runbook, and a stakeholder RACI and send it to everyone.
[05:47] Carlos Mendez: last question — any known limitations with model quantization or KV cache that might affect PHI workloads? i've seen some docs where KV cache is spelled out differently.
[05:57] Samir Patel: there's no PHI-specific limitation; we do have quantization profiles that may slightly affect quality — we recommend benchmarking with your prompts. KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) is supported but we will ensure cache separation and TTLs for multi-tenant scenarios; in Private there is no multi-tenant caching.
[06:12] Jamie Park: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the redlines and schedule the benchmark.
[06:18] Maya Thompson: thanks all. bye.
